title: The Ferry to Kadıköy
text:
My name is Elif. I live in Beşiktaş, and I work in Kadıköy. Every morning I take the ferry. I love the ferry. It is slow, but it is beautiful.

I buy a simit and a glass of tea on the ferry. The tea is hot and the simit is fresh. I sit next to the window and I look at the sea. The sea is blue and calm today.

There are many seagulls behind the ferry. A small boy throws a piece of simit, and a seagull catches it. Everybody laughs.

The trip takes twenty minutes. When we arrive, I am happy and ready for work.

questions.q: Where does Elif work?
questions.explain: Metinde “I work in Kadıköy” diyor: Beşiktaş'ta oturuyor, Kadıköy'de çalışıyor.

questions.q: What does Elif drink on the ferry?
questions.explain: “a glass of tea” = bir bardak çay. Simitle birlikte çay alıyor.

questions.q: Who catches the piece of simit?
questions.explain: Simidi küçük çocuk atıyor (throws), martı yakalıyor (catches).

title: Sunday Breakfast
text:
On Sundays my family has a big breakfast. We don't hurry on Sundays. My father goes to the bakery and buys fresh bread. My mother makes menemen with eggs, tomatoes and peppers.

I put the plates on the table. There is white cheese, black olives, honey, butter and jam. My little brother loves honey. He eats it with a spoon!

My grandmother pours the tea. She always asks, “Do you want more tea?” and we always say yes. We talk, we laugh and we eat for two hours.

After breakfast, we wash the dishes together. Sunday is my favourite day of the week.

questions.q: Who buys the bread?
questions.explain: “My father goes to the bakery” – babası fırına gidip ekmek alıyor.

questions.q: What does the little brother eat with a spoon?
questions.explain: “My little brother loves honey. He eats it with a spoon!” – balı kaşıkla yiyor.

questions.q: How long is the breakfast?
questions.explain: “for two hours” = iki saat boyunca. İngilizcede süre “for” ile anlatılır.

title: Saturday at the Bazaar
text:
Every Saturday there is a bazaar on our street. It opens early in the morning. I go there with my aunt. She carries a big shopping bag with wheels.

The bazaar is very noisy. The sellers shout, “Fresh tomatoes! Cheap cucumbers!” My aunt touches every tomato. She is very careful. She asks the price, and then she says, “It is too expensive.” The seller smiles and gives a better price.

We buy potatoes, onions, apples and a kilo of cherries. The cherries are sweet and dark red. I eat some on the way home.

The bag is heavy now, so I pull it for my aunt.

questions.q: When is the bazaar?
questions.explain: İlk cümle: “Every Saturday there is a bazaar” – her cumartesi kuruluyor.

questions.q: Why does the seller give a better price?
options: Because the aunt says it is too expensive
questions.explain: Teyze “It is too expensive” (çok pahalı) diyor, satıcı da gülümseyip daha iyi bir fiyat veriyor – tanıdık bir pazarlık!

questions.q: What colour are the cherries?
questions.explain: “sweet and dark red” – tatlı ve koyu kırmızı.

title: The Cat of Our Street
text:
There is an orange cat on our street. Her name is Pamuk. She doesn't have a home, but everybody on the street is her family.

In the morning, the grocer gives her milk. At noon, the woman on the second floor puts some food in a small bowl. In the evening, the children play with her in the park.

Pamuk sleeps in a box in front of the pharmacy. The pharmacist puts an old blanket in the box for her. In winter, it is warm and soft.

Pamuk is lazy and a little fat, but she is very friendly. When I come home from school, she runs to me and says, “Meow!” I think she says hello.

questions.q: Who gives Pamuk milk in the morning?
questions.explain: “In the morning, the grocer gives her milk.” – sabahları bakkal süt veriyor.

questions.q: Where does Pamuk sleep?
options: In a box in front of the pharmacy
questions.explain: “in front of the pharmacy” = eczanenin önünde. Kutuda, eski bir battaniyenin üstünde uyuyor.

questions.q: Which word describes Pamuk?
questions.explain: Metinde “lazy, a little fat, but very friendly” deniyor. Tembel ama çok cana yakın.

title: My New Neighbour
text:
We have a new neighbour. His name is Mr. Kaya. He is a teacher, and he is sixty years old. He lives alone with a lot of books and a small bird.

On his first day, my mother makes a plate of börek. I take it to his door. He opens the door and smiles. “Thank you very much! Come in, please,” he says.

His flat is full of plants and old photos. He shows me a photo of a little village near Trabzon. “This is my village. I was born there,” he says.

A few days later, he gives back the plate. It is not empty. There is a cake on it! In Turkey, we never give back an empty plate.

questions.q: What is Mr. Kaya's job?
questions.explain: “He is a teacher” – öğretmen. Meslek söylerken “a/an” kullanmayı unutma: a teacher.

questions.q: Where was Mr. Kaya born?
questions.explain: Fotoğrafı göstererek “This is my village. I was born there” diyor: Trabzon yakınındaki bir köy.

questions.q: What is on the plate when Mr. Kaya gives it back?
questions.explain: Tabak boş dönmüyor; üstünde kek var. Son cümle bir Türk geleneğini anlatıyor: boş tabak geri verilmez.

questions.q: “He lives alone” means…
questions.explain: alone = yalnız, tek başına. “lives alone” = yalnız yaşıyor.

title: A Bayram Visit
text:
Last Bayram, we drove from İzmir to Manisa to visit my grandparents. We left early in the morning because the roads are always busy during the holiday.

When we arrived, my grandmother was waiting at the door. I kissed her hand and put it on my forehead. She gave me some money in an envelope and said, “Buy yourself something nice.” My cousins were already there, and the house was very crowded.

All day, neighbours and relatives came and went. Every time the doorbell rang, my grandmother offered them coffee, chocolate and lokum. I helped her in the kitchen and carried the trays.

In the afternoon, my grandfather told us stories about his childhood. When he was young, children went from door to door and collected candy in a handkerchief.

We returned home late at night. I was tired, but I was also very happy.

questions.q: Why did the family leave early?
options: Because the roads are busy during the holiday
Because they wanted breakfast in Manisa
questions.explain: “because the roads are always busy during the holiday” – bayramda yollar hep yoğun olduğu için erken çıktılar.

questions.q: What did the grandmother give the writer?
questions.explain: Bayram harçlığı! “She gave me some money in an envelope” – zarfın içinde para.

questions.q: What did children collect in the grandfather's childhood?
questions.explain: “collected candy in a handkerchief” – mendile şeker topluyorlardı.

questions.q: “The house was very crowded” – Türkçesi hangisi?
questions.explain: crowded = kalabalık. was = -di (geçmiş zaman): “kalabalıktı”.

title: Balloons over Cappadocia
text:
For my thirtieth birthday, my husband gave me a surprise: a hot air balloon ride in Cappadocia. I was excited, but I was also a bit scared because I don't like heights.

The minibus picked us up from our hotel at five o'clock in the morning. It was still dark and very cold. At the field, the pilot explained the safety rules. Then we climbed into the basket with twelve other people.

Slowly, the balloon went up. Suddenly the sun came up, and I forgot my fear. Below us, there were valleys, strange rocks called fairy chimneys, and small villages. Around us, more than a hundred colourful balloons were flying in the sky.

The ride lasted one hour. When we landed, the crew gave us a glass of fruit juice and a small certificate. I am going to keep it forever.

questions.q: Why was the writer a bit scared?
options: She doesn't like her husband's surprises
She was late for the minibus
questions.explain: “because I don't like heights” – yükseklikten hoşlanmıyor. heights = yükseklik.

questions.q: What time did the minibus come?
questions.explain: “at five o'clock in the morning” – sabah saat beşte.

questions.q: What are “fairy chimneys”?
questions.explain: Metin açıklıyor: “strange rocks called fairy chimneys” – peri bacaları denilen tuhaf kayalar.

title: The Wrong Dolmuş
text:
Last month I started university in İzmir. On my first day, I wanted to go to the campus by dolmuş. A dolmuş stopped in front of me, and I got on quickly without reading the sign.

I passed my money to the man in front of me, and he passed it to the driver. That is how people pay in a dolmuş. After fifteen minutes, I looked out of the window. The sea was on my left. That was strange, because the campus is far from the sea.

I asked the woman next to me, “Excuse me, does this dolmuş go to the university?” She laughed kindly. “No, dear, it goes to Karşıyaka. You need to get off and take the one on the other side of the road.”

I got off at the next stop and crossed the road. I was forty minutes late for my first class, but the teacher was late too!

questions.q: How do people pay in a dolmuş, according to the story?
options: They pass the money to the driver through other passengers
They pay with a card at the door
They pay when they get off
questions.explain: Parayı öndeki kişiye uzatıyor, o da şoföre veriyor. “That is how people pay” = insanlar böyle ödüyor.

questions.q: Why did the writer think something was wrong?
options: The sea was on the left
questions.explain: Solunda deniz vardı; oysa kampüs denizden uzak (far from the sea).

questions.q: Where did the dolmuş go?
questions.explain: Kadın “it goes to Karşıyaka” diyor.

questions.q: “I got off at the next stop” – Türkçesi?
questions.explain: get off = inmek, get on = binmek. got, get'in geçmiş hâli.

title: A New Phone
text:
My old phone was very slow, and the battery died every afternoon. So last weekend I went to a shopping mall in Ankara to buy a new one.

The shop assistant was a young man called Burak. He showed me three phones. The first one was cheap, but its camera was bad. The second one was beautiful, but it was too expensive for me. The third one was perfect: a good camera, a big battery and a fair price.

“Can I pay in instalments?” I asked. “Yes, you can pay in six instalments with your credit card,” Burak said. He also explained the warranty. “It is valid for two years. Please keep the receipt.”

At home, I moved my photos and contacts to the new phone. It took almost an hour. Then I took a selfie with my cat and sent it to all my friends. The photo was really clear!

questions.q: What was the problem with the second phone?
questions.explain: “it was too expensive for me” – benim için çok pahalıydı. Kamerası kötü olan birincisiydi.

questions.q: How many instalments can the writer pay in?
questions.explain: “you can pay in six instalments” – altı taksit. “Two years” garantinin süresi.

questions.q: Why should the writer keep the receipt?
questions.explain: Burak garantiyi anlatırken “Please keep the receipt” diyor: garanti için fiş/fatura saklanmalı.

title: Snow Day in Erzurum
text:
Erzurum is one of the coldest cities in Turkey. In January, it often snows for days. Last winter, on a Tuesday morning, my mother woke me up with good news. “Schools are closed today because of the snow!”

I looked out of the window. Everything was white. The cars were under the snow, and the streets were empty. I put on two jumpers, a thick coat, gloves and a hat, and I went out with my sister.

We built a snowman in the garden. We used coal for his eyes and a carrot for his nose. Then the neighbours' children came, and we had a big snowball fight. My sister threw a snowball at me, but it hit our neighbour, Mr. Arslan! Luckily, he laughed and threw one back.

When we came inside, our hands were red and frozen. My mother made hot soup and we drank sahlep with cinnamon. It was the best day of the winter.

glosses.threw one back: o da bir tane geri attı

questions.q: Why were the schools closed?
questions.explain: “Schools are closed today because of the snow!” – kar yüzünden okullar tatil.

questions.q: What did they use for the snowman's nose?
questions.explain: Gözler için kömür (coal), burun için havuç (carrot) kullandılar.

questions.q: Who did the sister's snowball hit?
questions.explain: Kardeşi kar topunu yazara attı ama komşuları Arslan Bey'e çarptı (hit).

title: A Job Interview in Ankara
text:
Zeynep had been looking for a job for four months when she finally got an email from a logistics company in Ankara. They wanted to interview her for a customer relations position. The interview would be in English, because the company works with partners in Germany and the Netherlands.

The night before, she prepared answers to common questions, ironed her shirt and set two alarms. In the morning she took the metro to Kızılay and arrived twenty minutes early, which gave her time to calm down.

The interviewer, Mr. Demir, asked her to introduce herself. Zeynep talked about her degree in international trade and her internship at a shipping firm in Mersin. Then he asked a difficult question: “Tell me about a time you dealt with an angry customer.”

She took a deep breath and described a real situation. A container had been delayed at the port, and the client was furious. Instead of making excuses, she had called him every day with updates until the problem was solved. In the end, he had sent her a thank-you note.

At the end of the interview, Zeynep asked about training opportunities. Mr. Demir seemed impressed. A week later, her phone rang. She had got the job.

questions.q: Why was the interview in English?
options: Because Mr. Demir didn't speak Turkish
Because the company works with partners abroad
questions.explain: Şirket Almanya ve Hollanda'daki ortaklarla çalıştığı için mülakat İngilizceydi.

questions.q: What did Zeynep do when the container was delayed?
options: She called the client every day with updates
She asked her manager to call the client
questions.explain: “Instead of making excuses” – bahane uydurmak yerine, sorun çözülene kadar her gün arayıp bilgi verdi.

questions.q: “Arrived twenty minutes early” – what does it tell us about Zeynep?
questions.explain: Erken gelip sakinleşmek için zaman kazandı; önceki gece de hazırlık yapmıştı – iyi hazırlanmıştı.

questions.q: “A container had been delayed” – which tense is this?
questions.explain: had been + V3 = geçmişteki bir olaydan daha önce olan edilgen durum: “gecikmişti / geciktirilmişti”.

title: A Developer's First Day
text:
Can had dreamed of working at a tech company since high school. On Monday, he finally started as a junior developer at a start-up in Maslak that builds a food delivery app.

His team lead, Selin, welcomed him at the door with a laptop and a badge. “Don't worry about writing code today,” she said. “Today is for setting up your environment and meeting people.”

At ten o'clock there was a stand-up meeting. Everyone stood in a circle and said three things: what they had done yesterday, what they were going to do today, and whether anything was blocking them. Can was nervous, so he simply said, “I'm new, and I'm going to install everything.” People smiled and clapped.

After lunch, Selin assigned him a mentor, Mert, who showed him the code base and explained how they review each other's work. “Nobody merges code without a review,” Mert said. “And if you break something, it isn't a disaster. We fix it together.”

By the evening, Can had managed to run the app on his computer and had fixed a tiny spelling mistake on the login screen. It was a one-line change, but when it was approved, he felt like a real developer.

questions.q: What did Selin say Can should do on his first day?
options: Write as much code as possible
Set up his environment and meet people
questions.explain: “Today is for setting up your environment and meeting people.” – Bugün ortamını kurmak ve insanlarla tanışmak için.

questions.q: In a stand-up meeting, people say…
options: what they did, what they will do and what is blocking them
what they will eat for lunch
questions.explain: Metindeki üç şey: dün ne yaptıkları, bugün ne yapacakları ve önlerinde bir engel olup olmadığı.

questions.q: What was Can's first change?
options: A fix for a spelling mistake
questions.explain: “fixed a tiny spelling mistake on the login screen” – giriş ekranındaki küçük bir yazım hatasını düzeltti.

questions.q: What does Mert say about breaking something?
options: It isn't a disaster; they fix it together
questions.explain: “it isn't a disaster. We fix it together.” – felaket değil, birlikte düzeltiriz. Hata yapmak cezalandırılmıyor.

title: The Night Train to Kars
text:
Ece and her best friend Deniz had wanted to take the train from Ankara to Kars for years. Tickets for the sleeper cabins sell out in minutes, so they set an alarm for midnight on the day sales opened, and they managed to get one.

The journey takes about twenty-five hours. Before leaving, they packed snacks, a small kettle, a string of fairy lights and a good book each. Their cabin was tiny, with two narrow beds and a window, but they decorated it with the lights and felt at home.

As the train moved east, the landscape changed completely. The yellow fields of Central Anatolia slowly turned into mountains and frozen rivers. At some stations, the train stopped long enough for passengers to jump out, stretch their legs and take photos in the snow.

In the dining car, they met a retired railway worker who was travelling to visit his grandchildren. He told them that the route had once been a simple way for people to get home, not a tourist attraction. “Now young people come for the photos,” he joked, “but I am glad they discover the east.”

When they finally reached Kars, it was minus twenty degrees. They were exhausted, but both agreed it had been the best trip of their lives.

questions.q: Why did Ece and Deniz set an alarm for midnight?
options: Because the train left at midnight
Because tickets sell out very quickly
Because they wanted to see the stars
questions.explain: “Tickets for the sleeper cabins sell out in minutes” – biletler dakikalar içinde tükendiği için satış açılır açılmaz almaya çalıştılar.

questions.q: How did the landscape change?
options: From yellow fields to mountains and frozen rivers
questions.explain: İç Anadolu'nun sarı tarlaları yavaş yavaş dağlara ve donmuş nehirlere dönüştü (turned into).

questions.q: What did the retired railway worker think about young tourists?
options: He was glad they discover the east
He was angry about the photos
He wanted them to stay home
questions.explain: Şaka yollu “fotoğraf için geliyorlar” dese de “I am glad they discover the east” diyor – doğuyu keşfetmelerine seviniyor.

title: Looking for a Flat in İzmir
text:
When Ahmet got a job offer in İzmir, he had only three weeks to find a place to live. He spent his evenings scrolling through property websites, but most of the flats near his new office in Bayraklı were either too expensive or already rented.

A colleague advised him to walk around the neighbourhood instead. “Lots of landlords here don't advertise online,” she said. “They just put a sign in the window or tell the local grocer.” So on Saturday, Ahmet took the ferry across the bay and spent the whole day exploring the side streets.

In the afternoon, a grocer told him about a two-bedroom flat on the third floor of an old building. The landlady, Mrs. Nermin, showed him around. The kitchen was small and the bathroom needed new tiles, but the balcony had a view of the sea and the rent was reasonable.

Before signing the contract, Ahmet checked a few important things: whether the deposit was refundable, who would pay for repairs and how much the monthly building fee was. Mrs. Nermin answered every question patiently. She even offered to fix the bathroom before he moved in.

Two weeks later, Ahmet was drinking his morning coffee on the balcony, watching the ferries cross the bay.

questions.q: What problem did Ahmet have with the websites?
options: The flats were too expensive or already rented
There were no flats near the sea
questions.explain: “either too expensive or already rented” – ya çok pahalıydı ya da çoktan kiralanmıştı.

questions.q: How did Ahmet find the flat?
options: A grocer told him about it
questions.explain: İş arkadaşının tavsiyesiyle mahallede dolaştı; bir bakkal ona daireden bahsetti.

questions.q: Which of these is the “building fee”?
questions.explain: building fee = aidat. rent = kira, deposit = depozito.

questions.q: What did Mrs. Nermin offer to do?
questions.explain: “She even offered to fix the bathroom before he moved in.” – taşınmadan önce banyoyu yaptırmayı teklif etti.

title: The Family Baklava Shop
text:
Three generations of the Yıldız family have made baklava in the same small shop in Gaziantep. Every morning at four, Grandfather Hüseyin still rolls out the dough until it is so thin that you can read a newspaper through it.

His grandson Emre, who studied business administration in İstanbul, came home last year with a bold idea. “We should sell online and ship all over the country,” he suggested at dinner. His grandfather frowned. “Baklava is not a phone. It must be eaten fresh. If it arrives broken or dry, people will say the Yıldız family has lost its quality.”

Instead of arguing, Emre decided to experiment. For two months he tested different boxes and delivery companies, sending trays to friends in İzmir, Ankara and Trabzon and asking them for honest feedback. Most of the early boxes arrived damaged, but eventually he designed a package that kept the baklava cool and in one piece for two days.

A week after the first online order, a review arrived from a customer in Edirne, and the whole family gathered around the computer. Grandfather Hüseyin read the review out loud: “It tastes exactly like the baklava I ate in Gaziantep as a child.” He was quiet for a moment, then smiled. “Fine,” he said. “But I am still choosing the pistachios.”

questions.q: Why was Grandfather Hüseyin against selling online at first?
options: He was afraid the baklava would arrive broken or dry
He wanted to close the shop
questions.explain: “If it arrives broken or dry…” – baklavanın kırık ya da kuru ulaşmasından ve ailenin itibarının zedelenmesinden korkuyordu.

questions.q: How did Emre respond to his grandfather?
options: He argued with him every day
He tested boxes and asked friends for feedback
questions.explain: “Instead of arguing, Emre decided to experiment.” – tartışmak yerine denemeler yaptı ve arkadaşlarından dürüst geri bildirim istedi.

questions.q: What does “eventually” mean in this story?
questions.explain: eventually = sonunda, bir süre sonra. Dikkat: “eventual(ly)” Türkçedeki “eventüel / muhtemelen” anlamına gelmez!

questions.q: What does the grandfather's last sentence show?
options: He still wants to keep the quality in his hands
questions.explain: İnternet satışını kabul ediyor ama “fıstıkları hâlâ ben seçiyorum” diyerek kaliteyi kendi kontrolünde tutmak istiyor.
